key_insight: Charge-aware machine-learning potentials enable near-DFT modeling of CrSBr and reveal that sulfur vacancies can lower chromium Frenkel-pair migration barriers by up to 1.1 eV.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports large-scale studies of defect engineering and beam-induced structural changes in CrSBr for future magneto-optoelectronic applications.
method: Develop and benchmark Cr–S–Br machine-learning interatomic potentials, including charge-aware qNEP.
Use nudged elastic band calculations to assess vacancy-assisted chromium migration.
Calculate displacement thresholds to compare species susceptibility to electron-beam damage.
evidence_signal: qNEP achieves near-DFT accuracy for lattice constants, formation enthalpies, vacancy energetics, and anisotropic pressure response; displacement calculations identify Br as the most susceptible species.
watch_item: Accuracy beyond the benchmarked structures and defect environments remains to be established.
paper_title: Defects and Structural Evolution in CrSBr: Machine-Learning Potentials for Atomistic Simulations
